changelog.entry: New: Blueprint Swap. The Build Plan can turn your plan steps, Doctrine rules and next-run mutator picks into one short code to share, and a pasted code shows up as a faint ghost list you adopt piece by piece. Nothing is ever applied by itself and nothing leaves your device.

New: Governor Doctrines. Once Automation Basics is researched, a Doctrines panel lets you write up to three if/then rules for worlds you are not standing on (for example: on Mars, if ecology is below 30%, buy a Recycler; or if stock is above 2,000, start a trade route to the neediest world). The Governor Report shows which rule fired last on each world, and Try for 30 ticks tells you how often your rules would fire without changing anything. A new Prestige Tree node, Standing Orders, raises the limit to five.

New: prestige Eras. Your title badge now names your era (Pioneer, Steward, Architect, Custodian) next to your Prestige level, and each era gives the sky a quiet colour shift and a one-line tagline under the title. It is only a look, nothing in the rules changes, and Settings has an Era look switch to turn the colours and the tagline off.

New: field notes and a hidden Codex. Each world in the Overview now has a short note, and seven of them end with one odd sentence. Do what it hints at and a silly Codex entry appears in the Charter (a hint is one button away once the Codex shows up). Four new collector achievements too: Codex Keeper, Weather Watcher, Charter Member and The Great Works.

New: the Charter. A Mission Board posts three optional objectives at a time (such as banking Iron or terraforming a world a particular way); finishing one stamps the Charter for good with a small permanent yield bonus on that world, shown on its Overview card, and you can swap a mission for the next one for 100 of your biggest resource pile. The Charter also holds four late-game Megaprojects (Orbital Mirror, Ring Habitat, Dyson Sail, Deep Core Tap) built from resources of several worlds at once, with a progress ring each on the Overview and a secret epilogue line for building all four.

New: System Anomalies. Every five minutes of game time a short anomaly (one minute) changes the rules a little, always the same six in the same order: Comet Pass, Solar Flare, Meteor Shower, Magnetic Storm, Clear Skies and Dust Cloud, alternating a boon and a strain. A line under the toolbar says what is coming and for how long, and you can turn them off in Settings (Timed anomalies).

New: Mutators for New Game+. In the Prestige Tree, pick up to three optional rule twists for your next run (Thin Atmosphere, One-Way Trade, Blind Governor, Costly Machinery); each one pays an extra Prestige Point when you prestige out of that run, and a small symbol next to the title and a Run rules line on the share card show which are on. Nothing is random and you can change the picks before you prestige.

New: a Goals panel under the toolbar always shows the next three things to do (build an Auto-Miner, research a level, visit a world, terraform a world) with a progress bar for each, and the next goal appears as you finish one. Turn it off in Settings.

New: after you finish the system, the Epilogue and the Stats & Share panel have a Copy result button that copies one line, such as SOL, 100% terraformed, with your worlds, achievements and time played. Every achievement you have earned now has a Share button that copies a line you can paste anywhere, with the share of players who have it when that figure is available. The How to Play panel has a link to the new Credits page.

New: a Pause, 1x, 2x and 4x control sits under the toolbar (Space pauses or resumes, [ and ] change the speed). Faster only means the game ticks more often, never that anything is skipped, and nothing at all happens while it is paused. New: a setting, on by default, pauses the game while this browser tab is hidden and tells you when you come back; switch it off in Settings if you want it to keep running in the background.

New in SOL: Chain Reactions (do the right actions in the right order within a minute for a small bonus, seven to find, with hints), a rhythm bonus for steady clicking (up to +5%, can be switched off), a trophy shelf of your five newest achievements, a Governor mood line on every Governor Report card, a Splits page for your time per world against your personal best (switch on Show timing in Settings), and Copy as spreadsheet text on the Build Plan. Research buttons now light up as soon as you can afford a node. Two new achievements: In Rhythm and Chain Reactor.

New Desktop layout for wide windows with a mouse: the world you are on fills the screen with its panels beside it, every world's resource is a chip across the top, and Research, the Governor, the Overview, Stats and the rest open as windows from the icons and the Menu (Esc). Your save carries over; switch layouts from the opening screen or the Menu. The Classic layout is unchanged.
Stats: a personal-best 'Fastest full playthrough' (measured per run, kept for life). The welcome-back line now also reports machines built and hand-mined loads since your last visit (R-9, R-10).

Light theme polish, and the light/dark switch now lives in Settings ("Colour theme") instead of a floating pill. Research nodes, Governor priority buttons, prestige and status greens, amber warnings and dimmed captions were darkened for readable contrast on the light theme. Dark mode is unchanged (Y11b).

Deeper story: the captain's log now also records each world you finish terraforming, your first trade route and your first prestige as longer story beats, alongside first arrivals and achievements (W1).

Captain's log: a running story line under the title (latest entry) plus a collapsible log, recording your first arrival at each world and every achievement you earn. The existing Story pill turns it on and off (A25).

Community leaderboard: an opt-in 'fastest full completion' board in the Stats panel, ranked by the simulated time it took to terraform every world. Nothing is shared unless you tick the box while signed in (A29).

Research is now a real tree: about 20 nodes per level that split and rejoin, ending at Near Bodies and then Far Bodies, most with a small bonus (yield, cheaper miners, cheaper trade routes). Existing research progress converts to nodes (U10).

Hold to repeat: holding Mine or an Auto-Miner/Recycler Buy button now repeats it slowly (about 4 a second) so big buying sessions don't strain your hands. It never beats clicking manually, and it can be switched off in Settings.
Achievement cards now show "Earned by N% of players" once enough real save data exists for that achievement (site-wide goal, Z1/Z27b).
Added a keyboard-shortcuts help overlay: press ? to see it, Esc to close it or whichever panel is open (site-wide goal, Z4).
Settings panel: added a "Reset to Default" button that resets text size and reduce-motion back to their defaults in one click (site-wide goal, folded from A26).
Reset This World and Prestige/New Game+ now use the site's shared confirmation dialog instead of a plain browser popup.
The welcome-back toast now shows a real "+X worlds, +Y achievements since you were last here" delta for this browser, instead of just restating your current totals.
Settings panel added: text size (A-/A/A+) and a reduce-motion toggle, both persisted per-browser.
Colorblind-safety audit completed — no hue-only state encodings found, no change needed.

Achievements launched — 18-achievement catalog with an in-game panel, SOL is the reference integration for the whole hub.
Milestone 11: Full system endgame — 100% completion win-state and final balance pass. All 17 milestones complete.
Milestone 10: Gas giant buildings — reskinned building system, sky cities, Mars-material dependency.
Milestone 9e-9g: Pluto, Jupiter's Moons, and Saturn's Moons resource loops — Milestone 9 fully complete.
Milestone 9a-9d: research tier 2 framework, Moon/Venus/Asteroid Belt resource loops, governor + trade generalized to N planets.
Milestone 6-8: Mars resource loop, trade system v1, and per-planet terraforming.
Milestone 2-5: automation, global ecology system, research system v1, and planet travel + the governor system.
Milestone 1: core click loop launched — the very first playable version of SOL.
